newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower after new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower after new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures finished mostly lower on profit taking and hedge selling after posting new contract highs early. Feeders also held losses on profit taking after setting a new high in May early.

Live cattle posted a new contract high in April of 70.250 cents per lb and also in October and December before closing overall 0.225 cent higher to 0.400 lower with only April up at 69.950 cents. May feeder cattle set a new high of 72.500 cents and futures closed 0.325 to 0.600 cent lower with March off 0.475 at 68.725.
April live cattle remained buoyed by strong cash cattle prices despite the profit taking that developed, traders said.

Packers paid $68 per cwt for fed cattle Tuesday, $2 higher than last week's top prices. Packers' willingness to raise bids for cattle was linked to a recent surge in boxed beef values that lifted prices Tuesday to the highest levels since January 21, they said.
But commercial hedge interest added to the profit taking in back months to take those months lower.
Also, some sources said the rally may have run its course as more fed cattle will be available by June.
Cargill Investor Services bought late while E.D.&F. Man and R.J. O'Brien sold after buying early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses sold April 70 calls and December 72 calls while buying April 68 calls and June 64 calls. Commercial hedging developed late, buying June 64 puts and selling 67 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures started higher in tandem with live cattle on carryover demand but turned lower on profit taking and spillover from deferred live cattle contracts. Higher corn futures also weighed on the market, especially since feeders looked short term overbought technically, traders said.

E.D.&F. Man sold March and ADM Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man sold August and October early. Cargill Investor Services sold May and spread long August live cattle/short April feeder cattle and then bought April 1998 live cattle and sold November feeders late. Lind-Waldock bought October live cattle and sold May feeders, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.02 to $68.96 per cwt.
